title: NASCAR Cup Series Veteran Sounds Alarm Over O’Reilly Series’ Troubling Future
description: Denny Hamlin has raised concerns about the financial stability of the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series, warning that losing one major team could weaken the competition across the field.The 23XI Racing co-owner discussed the issue on his Actions Detrimental podcast, where he talked about Sheldon Creed’s move from Haas Factory Team to Sam Hunt Racing.Hamlin welcomed […] The post NASCAR Cup Series Veteran Sounds Alarm Over O’Reilly Series’ Troubling Future appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Denny Hamlin has raised concerns about the financial stability of the NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, warning that losing one major team could weaken the competition across the field.

The 23XI Racing co-owner discussed the issue on his Actions Detrimental podcast, where he talked about Sheldon Creed's move from Haas Factory Team to Sam Hunt Racing.

Hamlin welcomed the move as a positive step for Sam Hunt Racing but used it to explain the financial pressure facing teams in NASCAR's second-tier series.

He believes a small group of well-funded organizations provides much of the competitive equipment fans see each Saturday. If one of those teams withdraws, Hamlin warned, the series could struggle to maintain its current level of competition.

Hamlin praised Sam Hunt Racing for securing Creed, the current points leader, and described him as an experienced driver who could help the team compete.

"I think it's good for Sam Hunt. He gets a proven race winner. Sheldon Creed is a steady, very good driver. I think that's what that team needs too."

However, Hamlin also highlighted the challenges facing smaller NASCAR O'Reilly Series teams. Hamlin credited Sam Hunt Racing, Ryan Sieg, JR Motorsports and Joe Gibbs Racing for keeping the O'Reilly Series competitive, warning that losing any one of them could seriously weaken the field.

"And listen, God bless Sam Hunt, Ryan Sieg, Dale Jr., and Joe Gibbs because if any one of those dominoes fall, and that series looks like ARCA," Hamlin said.

He also mentioned Tommy Joe Martins' team and welcomed what he described as a positive move to Ford. Hamlin said he appreciated the work the organization puts into its equipment each week.

Hamlin said the financial challenges behind NASCAR O'Reilly Series competition help explain why drivers frequently move between teams.

Hamlin also highlighted JR Motorsports' importance to the series, warning that losing its five cars could leave a major gap in the competitive field.

"Yeah, I just, I'm telling you that series in my mind, it's just really fragile," Hamlin said. "Like if Dale Jr., for some reason, he's not going to, but like, could you imagine those five cars not on the grid? It's just, it's not good."

According to Hamlin, many drivers in the Saturday races pay team owners for their seats. This arrangement often forces drivers to compare financial offers rather than remain with organizations where they have established themselves.

"They're switching teams like musical chairs every year. And the unfortunate truth is that 80% of those drivers in the Saturday races are paying some sum of money to the team owner to drive those cars," Hamlin said.

He explained that team owners weigh competing offers, while drivers sometimes move elsewhere when they cannot meet the required financial terms.

Financial demands often push NASCAR O'Reilly Series drivers to switch teams, even when they have proven they can compete and win races.

Hamlin acknowledged that fans see a competitive product when they watch NASCAR O'Reilly Series races. However, he argued that the quality of the racing does not reflect the financial security of the organizations involved.

"I know it looks like the O'Reilly Series, from the fans' perspective, is the most solid series that NASCAR has, but I'm telling you it is the most fragile when it comes to finances," Hamlin said.

Hamlin believes top teams should prioritize proven drivers based on their ability to win races rather than how much money they bring to the organization. Instead, he argued, financial contributions from drivers play a major role in determining who gets those opportunities.

"Yeah, listen. The top 10 drivers in O'Reilly should be there because the owners just want them to go win races, but that is not the model that the O'Reilly Series is right now. I mean, that's just not the truth."

Hamlin's comments highlight the challenge facing NASCAR O'Reilly Series teams as they balance competitive equipment, sponsorship funding, and driver payments. While the series continues to deliver close racing, he warned that its financial foundation remains vulnerable if one of its leading organizations steps away.

title: Decision to stay at Celtic did not take long - O'Neill
description: Martin O'Neill suggests he was never close to leaving Celtic after a three-game losing streak, with the veteran manager stressing his "great enthusiasm" for the role.
fullText:
Martin O'Neill has suggested he was never close to leaving Celtic after a three-game losing streak, stressing his "great enthusiasm" for the role.

The 74-year-old signed a one-year deal to stay on as manager after two interim spells last season culminated in a league and Scottish Cup double.

Following two defeats by Rangers last month - either side of a 3-1 home defeat by Ferencvaros in the Europa League - O'Neill felt "it might be time to wrap it up".

However, he said the decision to carry on "didn't take that long" as he prepared for Sunday's Premiership visit to Motherwell.

"Obviously, I'm disappointed with the week that we had," he explained. "As long as the football club wanted me, I was happy to do it."

Three weeks have passed since a 1-0 home loss to Rangers, Celtic's first dropped points in the league.

"Leaving at this particular stage would have been poor," added O'Neill. "Deep down, obviously through the disappointment of losing the games and maybe with the international break coming up at the time, maybe it gave me a little bit of time to reflect.

"Had there been no international break, I probably wouldn't even have said what I said."

'Not Celtic' - O'Neill condemns Desmond protest

O'Neill 'just as determined' to lead Celtic

O'Neill spoke of his success last season, explaining "it gives you that spur to want to go and do it", as he looked forward to nine games over a 28-day period before the next international break.

"This is what you want to be involved in," he said. "Whether you're good enough to play European football might be another thing. But at least you want to be involved in it. So we go with it.

"I have belief in the team and I think that our focus should be to try to win the league."

O'Neill won seven trophies in his first period at Celtic between 2000-05 and said his love of the sport remains undiminished, even as it brings stresses and strains.

"I have great enthusiasm," he added. "I always have had a great enthusiasm for the game of football.

"I enjoyed last season in a strange sort of way, even though I sometimes say that I don't enjoy management - but I'm past the joking stage. You naturally get concerned for the games. I'm always worried about football matches."

title: Detroit Lions elevate DB for Panthers game
description: The Detroit Lions elevated a veteran safety for Week 4, giving the secondary more depth for their matchup with Panthers.
fullText:
The Detroit Lions announced on Saturday that they have elevated safety Jalen Mills for their Sunday night game against the Carolina Panthers in Week 4.

This is the second straight week Mills has been called up from the practice squad as the Lions navigate a bunch of injuries at safety. Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph remain on the physically unable to perform list, while Avonte Maddox and Thomas Harper landed on injured reserve this past week. The good news for the Lions is that Branch's return seems imminent.

"He's close. Yep, he's close," Lions coach Dan Campbell said earlier this week. "He's ready to go. [I'm] tired of listening to him. So, I mean that in a good way. Man, he's put in a ton of work, and he looks really good. He's close."

Mills joins starters Chuck Clark and Christian Izien, who played well last week against the Jets, but the Lions secondary remains a problem and has struggled through the first three weeks of the season.

Mills, who rejoined the Lions' practice squad ahead of Week 3, adds another experienced body(122 games, 92 starts) to a defense that needs some stability.

title: Lewandowski and De Bruyne shine in Nations League while Džeko plays his last international game
description: Veteran stars took center stage in the Nations League on Friday with Robert Lewandowski and Kevin de Bruyne leading Poland and Belgium to victories thanks to multi-goal performances.Italy also kept Zinedine Zidane from winning in his home debut as France coach, while Edin Džeko made his last international appearance.
fullText:
Veteran stars took center stage in the Nations League on Friday with Robert Lewandowski and Kevin de Bruyne leading Poland and Belgium to victories thanks to multi-goal performances.

Italy also kept Zinedine Zidane from winning in his home debut as France coach, while Edin Džeko made his last international appearance.

De Bruyne showed he can still dominate a match at age 35 when he scored Belgium's first two goals in a 3-0 win over Turkey in League A.

De Bruyne opened the scoring 10 minutes into the game in Liege when he played a one-two with Dodi Lukébakio and struck from near the edge of the area.

The Napoli playmaker curled home another goal with half an hour to play. Substitute Romelu Lukaku sealed the win over the Turks. Lukébakio hit the post twice.

"I try to lead by example for the younger players, and they follow easily," De Bruyne said. "I feel I can still contribute. I am enjoying myself, and that is the main thing."

Belgium made it two wins and a loss — which came to France — under new coach Mark van Bommel.

When Zidane's name was read out by the stadium announcer after the teams were announced, a roar filled Stade de France.

Things looked good for the home side when Michael Olise put France ahead in the 55th minute with a curling shot from 20 meters which went in off the crossbar.

But poor defending midway through the second half allowed Italy central defender Alessandro Bastoni to run through and clip a low shot inside the right post to secure a 1-1 draw.

France leads Group 1 with seven points, followed by Belgium with six, Italy with four and Turkey with zero.

Lewandowski scored a hat trick to lead a 6-0 demolition of 10-man Romania in League B.

The 38-year-old Chicago Fire striker earned and converted a 24-minute penalty when Romania defender Radu Dragusin was sent off for fouling him in the box.

Lewandowski made it 2-0 in the 47th from a pass by Nicola Zalewski and then rounded off the lopsided victory late with his third goal.

Edin Džeko finished his nearly 20-year-international career for Bosnia-Herzegovina in a 1-1 draw with Sweden also in League B.

Džeko, 40, debuted for his nation in June 2007. He finished with 152 appearances and 73 goals, making him the record holder in both categories for the tiny Balkan nation after helping it reach two World Cups.

Džeko was given an honor guard when he was subbed off in the 63rd, shortly after Viktor Gyökeres scored for Sweden. Kerim Alajbegović equalized in the 80th for the hosts.

Also in League B, Northern Ireland beat Ukraine 3-0 in Slovakia with Ciaron Brown scoring twice.

fullText:
The Cleveland Browns defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 on Thursday night, improving the team to 3-1 on the season. The Browns' early-season success has been one of the biggest surprises in the NFL this year, and it is in large part thanks to the massively improved play from veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson.

The FOX Sports Radio morning show, 2 Pros and a Cup of Joe, hosted by Brady Quinn, LaVar Arrington, and Jonas Knox, discussed the story surrounding the Browns on Friday morning.

"Credit due, hat off to (head coach Todd Monken)," Arrington said. "He has the Cleveland Browns at 3-1 after a divisional opponent in the Pittsburgh Steelers, who were coming off of a big victory over the Cincinnati Bengals. So give them credit. But I think this is honestly, potentially, this is more of an indictment on the Pittsburgh Steelers than it is a feel-good story for the Cleveland Browns.

“STOP throwing a pity party for what’s happened in the past for yourself. You won a game; make it about everyone besides YOU because, quite frankly, you’re on a really good team!”

– @Brady_Quinn on the Deshaun Watson PR spin. pic.twitter.com/Wab9BaPcmy

— FOX Sports Radio (@FoxSportsRadio) October 2, 2026

"I don't understand this need for a, well, feel-good story," Knox said. "I don't get it. What were the struggles? Let's just like break down the struggles. The struggles were: you had a fetish with the handhouse, and you weren't available. And then when you were available to play after suspension, you were injured. And then when you weren't injured, you were bad."

Quinn went on to make it clear that while he's happy for Browns' fans, he doesn't see why Deshaun Watson is throwing a "pity party" for himself.

"I feel good for the Cleveland fans. Yes. I feel good for a lot of those players," Quinn said. "I'm not sure what PR spin they're trying to put on or revisionist history they're trying to make. Anything that he endured in the past, he brought on himself. I mean, there's, there's not one part of the adversity he faced that he should have been solely responsible for.

"So like, here's the unfortunate part is we have— we're going to keep talking about this because they're going to keep bringing it up and we're going to have to keep addressing it, acknowledging it. Like, dude, stop throwing a pity party. For what's happened in the past for yourself. All right, you won a game, make it about the team, make it about everyone besides you, because quite frankly, you're on a really good team and it is about everyone besides you.

"Like, you're the quarterback, all right? This isn't Lamar Jackson in college running around carrying Louisville or at times carrying Baltimore. Like, you are there because— and you're being successful because of the help you have around you. So I just, I hope he stops with keep trying to get people to feel bad for him."

The Browns and Watson will next face the New York Jets.

Red Sox star Willson Contreras speaks up on 'data' and 'computers after series loss to Yankees appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

As the Boston Red Sox's 2026 season ended with a two-game sweep by the New York Yankees in the American League Wild Card Series, veteran catcher Willson Contreras made his frustration with the organization's data-driven approach clear after Wednesday's loss.

Contreras had momentarily given Boston a glimmer of hope in the sixth inning when he launched a Statcast-projected 387-foot solo home run to right-center with two outs. The blast ended a 26-inning postseason scoring drought for the Red Sox dating back to Game 2 of last year's Wild Card Series, also against the Yankees. However, New York answered with six runs in the bottom of the inning, turning the game into a 9-2 defeat.

Boston was outscored 18-2 across the two games and was eliminated before getting a chance to play in October. The loss also extended the Red Sox's streak to five consecutive seasons without postseason baseball at Fenway Park.

After the game, Contreras was asked about manager Chad Tracy's decision to remove starter Sonny Gray in the fifth inning. Gray had allowed six hits across 4 2/3 innings and surrendered only one run, a solo homer by Luis García Jr. He left after reaching 70 pitches with runners on the corners and two outs.

Tracy replaced Gray with left-handed reliever Erik Miller to face Cody Bellinger. Miller surrendered a run-scoring single to Bellinger before allowing another single to García. Gray had recorded a .180/.235/.280 slash line against hitters during their third time facing him this season, while Bellinger had been better against left-handed pitching than right-handed pitching. Contreras responded to the question about Gray by pretending to zip his mouth closed.

He was more direct when discussing Boston's broader reliance on data and technology.

"It's not enough when you have talent, or you have data, or you have computers telling you what to do, because this is baseball," said Contreras. "The data is here to help us but at the end of the day, you're going to need experience and veteran guys to win games. There's a lot of stuff that I would like to say, but I'll state it like that."

The comments came after the Red Sox's disappointing postseason exit and a regular season that featured major swings in performance. Boston fell into a 32-46 hole before going 32-5 from June 25 through August 7, including a franchise-tying 15-game winning streak.

The team then slumped during the final month amid injuries and offensive problems, which carried into the postseason. The Red Sox's bullpen also labored through a second consecutive difficult night against New York, while Garrett Crochet's return from shoulder and lat issues lasted less than an inning. Making his first appearance since April 25, Crochet failed to record an out and was charged with four runs.

title: Packers host veteran OL Kevin Zeitler on visit
description: The Packers might not be done adding to the offensive line. Veteran Kevin Zeitler was in Green Bay for a visit on Tuesday.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers are leaving no stone unturned in their search for much-needed help along the offensive line. According to the league's transaction wire, the Packers hosted veteran offensive lineman Kevin Zeitler, a Wisconsin native, for an official visit on Tuesday.

The Packers recently signed 2015 first-round pick Laken Tomlinson to the 53-man roster and 2020 first-round pick Mekhi Becton to the practice squad. Could Zeitler, a 2012 first-round pick who has made 213 career starts, be the next addition?

A reported visit suggests the Packers are strongly interested in signing the player, although nothing was official as of Tuesday afternoon.

Zeitler, now 36, has played for six NFL teams. He most recently played for the Tennessee Titans, starting 16 games for the team during the 2025 season. His contract expired following the 2025 season and he has not signed with a team for the 2026 season.

Zeitler has played over 14,000 career snaps at right guard, his preferred position. The Packers have started Jacob Monk at right guard during the first three games, and Monk has struggled mightily, allowing 11 pressures, including one sack and five quarterback hits, per PFF.

Even as a 35-year-old with the Titans last season, Zeitler allowed only 16 total pressures and committed only four penalties across 909 snaps, per PFF.

If signed, Zeitler could give the Packers a reliable veteran presence at right guard, while Tomlinson -- who has played the majority of his career at left guard -- could handle the other side while Aaron Banks is out with knee and toe injuries.

title: Keenum stars for Bears on first start since 2023
description: Veteran quarterback Case Keenum throws for two touchdowns and rushes for another as the Chicago Bears beat the Philadelphia Eagles in the NFL.
fullText:
Veteran quarterback Case Keenum starred on his first start for almost three years as the Chicago Bears handed the Philadelphia Eagles their first defeat of the season.

Starting his first NFL game since December 2023, the 38-year-old threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for another as the Bears won 27-7 at Soldier Field in Chicago.

It is the first time he has thrown multiple touchdowns in a game since October 2019, while he is also the oldest player to score a rushing touchdown for the Bears.

Third-choice quarterback Keenum, an NFL journeyman playing at his eighth franchise, was called into action because Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring injury last week and his back-up Tyson Bagent then suffered a concussion.

Wide receiver Kalif Raymond, who scored a touchdown, said: "He was like, 'I may not be a cowboy, but this is definitely not my first rodeo'. [There's] a lot of confidence in him; a lot of confidence in himself.

"He practises, preps every week, but particularly this week. We didn't expect anything different from him."

Keenum's first drive resulted in a touchdown for Luther Burden III, and Cairo Santos added a 29-yard field goal before Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts rushed for a touchdown to cut the Bears' half-time lead to 10-7.

Santos added a second field goal early in the third quarter before the Bears scored two touchdowns among 17 unanswered points.

The Bears defence limited the Eagles to 248 total yards and claimed two interceptions - one from Jalen Hurts and another from his back-up Andy Dalton, who came in for four snaps while Hurts was checked for a potential concussion in the second quarter.

title: Nottinghamshire sign Sussex wicketkeeper Simpson
description: Nottinghamshire sign veteran wicketkeeper John Simpson from Sussex on a deal that will keep him at Trent Bridge beyond his 40th birthday.
fullText:
Nottinghamshire have signed veteran wicketkeeper John Simpson from Sussex on a deal that will keep him at Trent Bridge beyond his 40th birthday.

Simpson joins the East Midlands side on a two-year deal encompassing both the County Championship and One-Day Cup formats.

The 38-year-old has amassed more than 14,000 runs across first-class and List A competitions during a 17-year professional career in which he spent more than a decade at Middlesex - where he won the 2016 Division One title - before he went on to join Sussex in 2024.

He captained Sussex to promotion from Division Two of the County Championship and helped them reach T20 Blast Finals Day in his first year with club.

Simpson, who earned three One-Day International caps for England in 2021, scored 581 County Championship runs in the 2026 season - the first time he fell under the 1,000-run mark in his three years at Hove - as Sussex finished third in the table and just ahead of Notts.

He described his years with Sussex as "some of the most enjoyable and rewarding of my career" but went on to say he was "excited" by the "new challenge" at Nottinghamshire.

His move to Trent Bridge brings an end to Kyle Verreynne's time with the East Midlands side, the South African having helped the club to the 2025 County Championship title during his three-year tenure.

Verreynne's time at Trent Bridge was cut short in September when called up by Cricket South Africa, forcing Notts to pick up New Zealand's Mitchell Hay on a short-term deal to see out their ultimately failed attempt to retain the title.

Notts head coach Peter Moores hailed Simpson as "a quality" wicketkeeper and batter that boasts "a proven track record".

"It's a double-edged sword because we've loved having Kyle, and he's been fantastic for us," Moores told the club website. "The big difference by having John to play the same role is the flexibility it will give us with our second overseas spot moving forward."

Adrian Harms, BBC Radio Sussex's cricket reporter

Paul Farbrace took a season to assess the weaknesses in the Sussex squad when he took the reins in 20023.

His assessment was stark, Sussex had forgotten how to win, and despite an array of young developing talent, they needed, in his words, 'some gnarled old pros' to bring the best from the squad.

Enter John Simpson and the rest is history - it's doubtful there have been many more shrewd signings in recent Championship history.

As captain he led by example, immediately guiding Sussex to promotion as champions after a long nine-year absence from Division One, and the following season leading the club to a highly creditable fourth place finish.

This season, with the ramifications of financial mismanagement rumbling around the club, he has, as club captain, helped guide Sussex to their highest finish for 12 years.

His fitness has been exemplary, having not missed a Championship match during his time at the club, scoring an astonishing 11 centuries, averaging a shade over 50, and claiming 144 dismissals behind the stumps.

Simpson's contribution to Sussex has been immense over the past three seasons, his departure a huge blow to the club, but his place in Sussex history is assured, and he will always be welcomed back to Hove with open arms.

Matthew Stafford made NFL history for an unwanted reason as the Los Angeles Rams suffered a stunning 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos. The veteran quarterback threw his 33rd career pick-six, surpassing Brett Favre for the most in league history.

The record-breaking play came with the Rams holding a 19-16 lead in the fourth quarter. Talanoa Hufanga jumped in front of a pass intended for Kyren Williams and returned the interception 66 yards for a touchdown, giving Denver its first lead of the night.

The mistake was particularly costly because Los Angeles had controlled much of the game early. The Rams carried a 16-0 advantage into halftime before the Broncos mounted a second-half comeback, turning the contest into a back-and-forth battle that remained undecided until the final seconds.

Stafford did not allow the interception to derail him immediately, responding with a 48-yard touchdown pass to Konata Mumpfield on the next possession. title: The RUNDOWN: Everything you need to know about the Bears in Week 3 against the Eagles
description: LAKE FOREST, Ill. — Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor is just one month older than quarterback Case Keenum. So he has a deep appreciation and respect for what the veteran...
fullText:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. — Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor is just one month older than quarterback Case Keenum.

So he has a deep appreciation and respect for what the veteran did this past week to prepare for the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football.

"I just haven't practiced in 15 years and I don't know that I could get up and do that every single day," Taylor said.

With that said, here's everything you need to know from the podium to the injury report to the Bears locker room before kickoff in Week 3.

Tyson Bagent officially cleared concussion protocol on Sunday. Case Keenum got the majority of the practice work this past week but it's always possible that Bagent plays.

"Since it's progressed along, he was able to be in meetings (Friday) and now he's in practice (Saturday), and so he's right on track to be right where he needs to be," Ben Johnson said on Saturday. "And I think mentally he's going to be in a good spot for what we're asking to do."

Johnson has talked too much about the significance of practice reps for all players in the past to overlook how important they were for Keenum over the past few days. But Bagent also had good moments against the Minnesota Vikings that he can build upon.

"I thought he did a great job giving us an opportunity at the end of the game," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. "You are facing that (Vikings) defense. It's a tough situation. He gave us an opportunity to get down there. Obviously, it goes without being said, we'd like to have maximized both those possessions that end up inside the 12-yard line better than we did. But I thought in terms of being a backup thrown into a tough situation, he did a great job giving us an opportunity."

Caleb Williams was ruled out for Monday night but his status remains something to watch throughout Monday. ESPN/NFL Network reported that Williams is dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring pull and could miss three or four weeks.

My understanding from the start was that Williams was always looking at a multi-week absence. Playing against the Eagles was never a realistic option. The question was how quickly Williams would start to recover and progress.

As my colleague Adam Hoge pointed out on X on Sunday, the clearest indicator of the severity of Williams' injury will come at 3 p.m. on Monday – the deadline for roster moves before kickoff.

Placing Williams on injured reserve would guarantee a four-week absence but also provide the Bears with an available roster spot – which they could use with linebacker Noah Sewell and defensive lineman Shemar Turner nearing their activations from the PUP list.

Here's one thing for certain: the long-term health of Williams will be prioritized. The Bears will not rush him back. The organization can still hope for the best with Williams but it also has planned for the worst. The Bears can turn to Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum.

It might be different if Keenum was just added to the roster with Caleb Williams (QB1) and Tyson Bagent (QB2) ailing. But Keenum has played an integral role behind the scenes since joining the Bears in April 2025.

"It's always fun, kind of get to work with a vet," tight end Cole Kmet said. "Obviously, they've seen so much and done so much, and how many times has he set a play call in the huddle? So it's cool to kind of get that vibe from him. And I know he's super excited about the opportunity, all that type of stuff."

Keenum took the first-team reps during the Bears' prep for the Eagles.

"The way he commands everything, he's been doing it for a long time," running back D'Andre Swift said. "So he's been great."

Keenum is part of the Bears' investment in Williams but also the position overall.

"(It's) just his professionalism," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. "He's obviously done it a really long time and at a high level, and he's been through kind of every role you can be in in a quarterback room, from undrafted to a franchise guy to a backup to an up-and-down starter. And so I think all those lessons have really kind of molded him into the quarterback he is today. He's probably not the same quarterback he was 12, 13 years ago, five years ago.

"And then … he's been with us since Day 1, so he's watched this thing get built, he's had input on the way we've done things. And now it's really cool to see him get a little bit more opportunity here in practice and see how he handles it. If his opportunity comes, I don't think anybody has any doubt he'll be ready for the moment."

He didn't practice Wednesday, Thursday (estimation) or Friday because of soreness in his hip. But he was back in action on Saturday.

Santos doesn't have an injury designation for Monday night.

"I just felt some soreness after the (Vikings) game," Santos told reporters. "I felt good that it wasn't an injury-related thing and I'm thankful for coach Johnson and (special teams coordinator Richard Hightower) for letting me rest. I don't think I've ever had a rest day. But maybe it's that point in my career that after a rainy game, kicking a lot of wet balls, they're heavier. I felt like my body just felt a little sore. I just rested and then felt good (Saturday)."

It's because he's "Miami tough," according to Ben Johnson.

"I was fortunate to be down there for seven years, and so I do think there's something in the water down there," Johnson said. "Guys are a little bit different in terms of how they're brought up. And so it's good. I said it at the end of training camp, we have a roster full of guys that are fighting – fighting to be on that grass and be on the field and help their teammates win."

Stevenson was initially deemed week-to-week with a hamstring injury, which he suffered against the Vikings. But he returned to practice on Friday and now he doesn't have an injury designation for Week 3.

It's been an injury-filled few weeks for Stevenson. He got banged up in training camp at Halas Hall and later during the joint practice against the Tennessee Titans. Stevenson was later evaluated twice for a concussion in Week 1 against the Carolina Panthers, the second time because of a stinger.

Last year was last year regardless of the 281 rushing yards produced by the Bears in Philadelphia.

Last week, Swift felt like he left yards – and definitely a touchdown because of his fumble – on the field against the Vikings.

"I feel like I missed a couple out there, but (it's) a different style of defense that was kind of getting thrown at us," Swift said. "Another opportunity to make it right (on Monday)."

Week 3 is Week 3 regardless of opponent.

"(We) just so happen to play the Eagles," Swift said.

Mannion is in his first year as the Eagles' offensive coordinator. He's a first-time playcaller. He spent the past two years with the Green Bay Packers as an offensive assistant and then quarterbacks coach.

A former quarterback, Mannion is also not far removed from his own playing career. His last stint came in December 2023 on the Seattle Seahawks' practice squad.

Allen's first season as a defensive coordinator came in 2011 with the Denver Broncos.

"We're obviously defending the scheme and as we're going through this, we're trying to evaluate, 'OK, what is Philly as it's been for the last few years? What are the new wrinkles that Sean's bringing over with him?' And (it's) just trying to see how they're going to attack the game," Allen said. "But we've really got to defend the plays and the formations that are set before us. My job will be to try to get a feel for what their plan is and how they're trying to attack us and then we've got to be able to adjust to whatever that might be."

Bears vs. Eagles Predictions: What's left in the tank for QB Case Keenum?

From Week 1 to Week 2, Roush's snaps on offense increased from 12 to 20 but dropped from 28 to nine on special teams.

Roush wasn't set on first-and-10 on the Minnesota Vikings' 30 when tight end Colston Loveland had a 14-yard catch. His illegal shift wiped out the gain. It also was the start of four penalties in five plays for the Bears.

Roush also had a drop in the red zone four plays before Caleb Williams suffered his hamstring injury.

On special teams, it first appeared that Roush was to blame for the blocked field goal by the Vikings. But a closer look revealed that the snap count was off. Veteran long snapper Scott Daly later replaced rookie Beau Gardner on the roster.

But will Roush's playing time come next?

"It's not the only phase he played on, and he graded out extremely well on kickoff return. He graded out extremely well on punt," special teams coordinator Richard Hightower said. "So he's got to keep growing him. He's not on punt return yet or on kickoff last game. He was the first game. He did an outstanding job on kickoff the first game. So he's a young player that we're developing. He cares. He's working his tail off, and we'll continue to develop him. So that's not the only thing he does. We all got to be better, alright. So I'm not going to single out, Sam. We all got to be better."

The team won't give up on developing rookie Beau Gardner.

But some stability was needed after the miscues in Week 3.

"He's a good friend," kicker Cairo Santos told reporters. "We stayed in touch, even trying to get him back here in free agency and helping him get other opportunities out there. It just felt like riding a bike when he came out there and executing our kicks (Saturday) and just kind of getting that rhythm again."

And it won't include Ozzy Trapilo quite yet despite his own progress.

The idea behind it is to keep Braxton Jones fresh for late in games. Backup Theo Benedet has played 38 snaps in two weeks.

"We'll see how the game goes," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. "We've kind of got a plan going into every single week. We'll discuss it as a staff early in the week, kind of see how it shakes out, and then we'll stamp it somewhere along the week and going into the game. We'll determine whatever gives us the best opportunity to win.

In two games, he has just one catch for three yards on five targets.

"I think obviously we want the ball," Loveland said after practice on Wednesday. "Everyone in here wants the ball. We're here for a reason and we want to make plays and help our team win. But there's other ways to make plays on the ground in the run game. I'm just doing what I'm asked, and like we were talking about, there's going to be opportunities, so I just gotta take full advantage when it arises."

That said, it's time to just throw the film of Week 2 out and focus on the Eagles.

"I don't think it's realistic to think anybody's going to air the ball out the way it went last week in the pouring rain," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said.

fullText:
Two veteran FBI agents overseeing counterterrorism operations in the nation’s capital have been removed from their jobs and reassigned over the handling of an investigation involving Katie Miller, the conservative podcaster and wife of senior White House adviser Stephen Miller, according to two people familiar with the move.

Michael Burgwald, the special agent in charge of counterterrorism matters at the FBI’s Washington Field Office, and his deputy, Courtland Rae, were ousted from their positions by bureau leadership after investigators determined that allegedly harassing phone calls Katie Miller received from unknown individuals did not warrant further investigation, the sources said.

The field office team that reviewed the reported harassing calls determined they did not meet the threshold required for an FBI investigation, and no nexus to terrorism was identified, the sources said. This decision did not sit well with bureau leadership, and the two senior field office agents were removed from their positions, according to the sources.

Since taking office last year, FBI director Kash Patel — a fierce loyalist of President Donald Trump — has fired, demoted, or forced into retirement countless career employees who handled past investigations into Trump and his allies. Many of those forced out have filed lawsuits seeking reinstatement.

In a statement on an official FBI “Rapid Response” social media account established to tout the agency and respond to critics, Darren Cox, the senior executive who oversees the bureau’s DC office, confirmed the ousting of Burgwald and Rae, but denied the order came from Patel.

“This was a personnel decision made at the Washington field office level alone based on our constant evaluation of mission needs,” Cox said. “Any suggestion otherwise is false.”

CNN is attempting to locate contact information for Burgwald and Rae. The decision to remove them from their positions has riled many rank and file FBI employees who have been critical of personnel moves they view as highly politicized, sources said.

Burgwald graduated from the United States Military Academy West Point and was the recipient of FBI investigative awards, while Rae similarly rose through the ranks of the organization after a lengthy career in national security, sources said.

The reassignment of the two senior officials was first reported by Bloomberg Law.

CNN has reached out to the White House for comment. In a statement to Bloomberg Law, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said Stephen and Katie Miller had no interaction with Burgwald or Rae, adding, “Senior leadership at the FBI determined they were stifling investigations into very serious threats and made a unilateral decision to remove them.”

Still, there is a history of the Millers expressing their displeasure at the FBI’s handling of personal incidents they viewed as threatening in nature. According to people familiar with an incident last year, the couple grew irate with FBI officials over pushback by career agents to use bureau resources to investigate paper flyers critical of Stephen Miller that were posted in the family’s neighborhood. Like several senior Trump officials, the couple later moved into military housing.

CNN’s Aleena Fayaz contributed to this report.

title: Internal DOJ charts show agency bleeding staff as caseloads surge
description:
A drastically diminished Justice Department workforce is struggling to keep up with its civil side caseloads, according to documents obtained by The Hill and NewsNation.
A series of charts, apparently inadvertently shared and then recalled, show how the number of attorneys within the civil division has plummeted under the Trump administration.
The charts substantiate a dynamic long suspected: that the Department of Justice (DOJ) would not be able to swiftly replace a crew of veteran attorneys after a wave of firings and resignations.
fullText:
A drastically diminished Justice Department workforce is struggling to keep up with its civil side caseloads, according to documents obtained by The Hill and NewsNation.

A series of charts, apparently inadvertently shared and then recalled, show how the number of attorneys within the civil division has plummeted under the Trump administration.

The charts substantiate a dynamic long suspected: that the Department of Justice (DOJ) would not be able to swiftly replace a crew of veteran attorneys after a wave of firings and resignations.

Stacey Young, who founded the DOJ alumni group Justice Connection, described the staff turnover as a “massive exodus.”

“The workload has skyrocketed, particularly in the civil division offices that have lost the most lawyers. So what we’re seeing is that the lawyers who are left are overworked, stressed out, many have lost those who led their office because they were pushed out by this administration. And because of the difficult circumstances under which they’re working, I expect that the rate of departures won’t slow down anytime soon,” she told The Hill.

“Putting out this data seems to me like a desperate cry for help. It seems like the civil division knows how badly it needs more funds to hire more lawyers to make up for the purge of longstanding experts that they caused.”

According to the Office of Personnel Management, the Justice Department has lost roughly 10,000 workers since the start of the Trump administration, a metric that includes component agencies like the FBI and the Federal Bureau of Prisons.

In graph after graph, the charts track data from the start of the Trump administration through August, showing a significant decline in civil division staff as caseloads have steadily ticked up.

DOJ defended the workload, saying it has hired new staff.

“The Civil Division is working every day to advance and defend the President’s agenda in court, and it is winning. Since the start of this Administration, the Civil Division has hired over 200 new attorneys with many 

“Civil Division attorneys have achieved countless wins in courts across the country and secured billions of dollars in fraud recoveries for the American people,” they added.

One chart reviewing impact on each branch within the division detailed how caseload was skyrocketing — with work for the commercial litigation branch jumping a whopping 84 percent per attorney, while lawyers in the Office of Immigration Litigation saw their workload jump 63 percent.

Attorneys who work on appeals saw their caseloads jump 54 percent while lawyers in the federal programs branch — those who work on defending executive orders among other administration priorities — saw their workloads jump 44 percent.

The number of attorneys in the federal programs branch dropped from 113 to 71 just within the first few months of the Trump administration. A jump in cases has largely settled to around 1,000, but they are being handled by a diminished team.

Jennifer Ricketts, a former Justice Department attorney who led the federal programs branch, said the swift exodus shows how many longtime attorneys who defended presidential priorities across administrations likely began looking for a new job as soon as President Trump won the election.

“They were aware of how much in the first Trump administration they tried to stretch the law and put us in positions where we struggled to make sure we satisfied our professional responsibilities and folks did not want to have to go through that exercise again,” she said of the branch.

“You don’t get jobs really quickly. So they had already started looking after the election, so it was not tied to any specific decision. It was the anticipation of what they may do, especially given how aggressive they said they were going to be and how aggressive we had seen them be in Trump one …. I think folks knew maybe not the scope of what was coming, but they knew none of it was going to be pleasant.”

One of the other most significant declines in staffing — combined with one of the highest rises in cases — was in the Office of Immigration Litigation, which has seen cases surge amid Trump’s pledge to carry out the largest mass deportation operation in history.

The Office of Immigration Litigation handles both individual immigration cases being heard at the Board of Immigration Appeals as well as immigration matters brought in federal district court, such as habeas corpus cases brought by migrants being held in detention. Habeas petitions have soared alongside detention rates as the administration has largely cut off access to bond hearings.

One former staffer from the immigration office noted the steady decline in staff in that branch, with attorneys going from 320 down to 243 as cases climbed from roughly 7,700 to nearly 9,500.

“We never had attrition like we’ve had. There’s been a lot of reasons for that,” the former staffer said.

Early in the administration, the Justice Department moved the branch’s leader to a new sanctuary city task force, and the Justice Department later made headlines for firing Erez Reuveni, a longtime Office of Immigration Litigation staffer, after he acknowledged in court that Kilmar Abrego Garcia had been mistakenly deported.

“When our colleague Erez Reuveni got fired, I think there were a lot of people that were saying, ‘If that could happen to him that could happen to any of us,’” the former staffer continued. “And I think that people just started looking, and you know, workload’s gone up. The office has sort of tried to recover from those blows … But it’s been increasingly challenging for people to do that. I think there’s a lot of unhappy people.”

“With caseload going up and the resources going down, it just makes it challenging,” they added.

Also surprising is the attrition among appellate staff attorneys, though their ranks have been rising over the last several months.

“It’s a very plum section, very elite section, and if folks leave there, they would often go to the solicitor general’s office or some other very prestigious placement,” Ricketts said, referencing the team of attorneys for the solicitor who argue before the Supreme Court.

While staffing in that branch hasn’t dipped as much as others, their caseload has increased substantially because the Trump administration has been appealing so many of its losses in court.

Though now down six attorneys from the 61 it began with, the number of appealed cases went from around 780 at the start of the administration to more than 1,100 last month.

“They will appeal everything. I mean, it does not appear to be an administration that takes losses. They do not seem to be worried about creating bad law in the court of appeals. They seem to be pursuing a very aggressive interpretation of executive branch authority, and so they are willing to roll the dice and take it up,” Ricketts said.

“I think my sense is they have a sense that the Supreme Court is willing to accept more of those ideas, what would have been considered extreme ideas, than we ever imagined, and so why not?”

Similarly to the Office of Immigration Litigation, the commercial litigation branch has also seen a consistent loss in staff — dropping from 350 at the start of the administration down to 289 — while caseloads have jumped from around 13,000 to nearly 19,000.

It’s hard to know what has driven the surge in caseload in the branch, which handles a wide variety of matters from cases where the government has a financial interest to intellectual property to those who represent the U.S. in cases in foreign courts.

But it does include two areas where there has been more active litigation.

The commercial litigation branch includes fraud — a topic of great interest to the Trump administration as it probes entitlement programs.

It also handles cases before the Merit Systems Protection Board, the quasi judicial board responsible for reviewing federal employee workplace challenges, including wrongful termination cases that have surged as the Trump administration pushed to reduce the size of the government.

After the email with the charts was sent last week, it was quickly recalled.

Sources suspect the graphs are preparation for the next budget cycle.

“Somewhere along the line, somebody in the division or the department is going to use this data to justify asking for more resources,” the former Office of Immigration Litigation staffer said.

They noted that none of the graphs start its axis at zero, a choice that emphasizes the rise in cases and fall in staff.

“They ginned up the charts to make that visually apparent,” they said.

The Justice Department has already made efforts to recruit more staff. In May, the department promised something largely unheard of in the federal government — a $25,000 signing bonus to those joining the civil division.

But it’s unclear if that’s working.

“DOJ had never given signing bonuses to try to attract applicants. These jobs were some of the most competitive legal jobs in the field. The fact that they’re now having to provide financial incentives for people to apply shows you just how desperate they are,” Young said.

“And we know that job openings that used to attract hundreds or thousands of applications are now attracting almost none.”

The Justice Department took a number of actions shortly after Trump took office that flushed staff and prompted headlines.

In the criminal division, the Justice Department fired those who had worked on cases involving Trump. In the civil division, many branch leaders were reassigned to take on unrelated work. The U.S. pardon attorney lost her job after she refused to certify that actor Mel Gibson should have his gun rights restored. And still more attorneys sought and gained jobs outside the department or availed themselves of a government buyout spearheaded by Elon Musk.

At the beginning of the administration, the Justice Department also withdrew offers to recent graduates who had been given entry level jobs through the prestigious Attorney General’s Honors Program, cutting off a pipeline of young attorneys from top schools who then rise through the ranks of the department.

“It reflects what we’ve been saying all along. This situation is untenable when you have an office that is experiencing a surge of cases because of this administration’s lawless conduct at a time when lawyers are fleeing the department. The administration won’t be able to defend itself in court,” Young said.

“DOJ lawyers, in the best of times, are overworked. Their workloads right now have increased exponentially, especially when it comes to civil division lawyers, and as their workloads continue to increase, more will leave, and the problem will just keep getting worse and worse.”

title: Phillies’ 7-Year Veteran Celebrates Rare MLB Feat With New Team
description: The Philadelphia Phillies have received a remarkable update on a long-time pitcher who left the organization.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Phillies entered the season with one of baseball's deepest starting rotations and the club has managed some turbulence and changes to retain that strength amid another playoff push.

With Cristopher Sanchez setting a franchise record earlier this season, Zack Wheeler fighting through a return from offseason surgery and Aaron Nola and Andrew Painter finding their strides, Philadelphia's rotation depth has remained a significant part of its postseason plans.

Under president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski, starting pitching has long been the Phillies' calling card. And that included the career start of a player who has now earned a notable career accomplishment with his new team.

Former Mets Backstop Suddenly Ends Career Just 8 Days Before Season Finale

Zach Eflin, who spent the first seven seasons of his career with the Phillies before moving on to the Tampa Bay Rays and then the Baltimore Orioles, has officially reached 10 years of MLB service time.

The Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) marked the occasion with an announcement on social media.

The milestone carries particular significance because reaching a decade of service requires much more than simply having major league talent. Players must remain healthy and productive enough to spend years in the majors while navigating injuries, roster decisions and the natural turnover of professional baseball.

When it comes to Eflin, many Phillies fans will take the moment to remember his dependability and contributions across many years in Philadelphia.

"Throughout history, fewer than 10% of Players have possessed the combination of talent, health, resilience, perseverance and good fortune to achieve the feat," MLBPA noted in the announcement. "Eflin was selected by San Diego in the first round of the 2012 draft and debuted with the Phillies four years later. Eflin spent his first seven seasons in Philadelphia before stints in Tampa Bay and Baltimore. The Florida native has pitched in over 200 games and accumulated more than 900 strikeouts."

Eflin's Philadelphia tenure included several different stages of his development, including the start of what became a standout career in the majors.

Eflin's biggest transformation came after he moved away from an approach centered on overpowering hitters and instead leaned more heavily on his sinker and curveball, thanks in large part to the Phillies' development system. That adjustment helped him become a more effective major league starter, including a 2020 season in which he posted a 3.97 ERA and 10.9 strikeouts per nine innings.

Injuries interrupted his time with Philadelphia, including season-ending knee surgery in 2021. But he later became an important part of the Phillies' 2022 postseason bullpen, posting a 3.38 ERA across 10 and two-thirds playoff innings.

After the 2022 season, Eflin left Philadelphia and signed a three-year, $40 million contract with the Rays. Now, more than a decade after being drafted, the former Phillies pitcher has reached one of baseball's most exclusive career milestones.

title: ‘People Around the League Will Be Monitoring’ — NBA Insiders Make Feelings Clear on Kyrie Irving’s Uncertain Future With Mavericks
description: The Dallas Mavericks might have to make a decision regarding their veteran star soon. The team already has the new face of its franchise in Cooper Flagg, which places Kyrie Irving’s future with the team into question.
fullText:
The Dallas Mavericks might have to make a decision regarding their veteran star soon. The team already has the new face of its franchise in Cooper Flagg, which places Kyrie Irving's future with the team into question.

NBA Insiders Tim MacMahon and Marc J. Spears discussed the future and the uncertainties surrounding it.

The 2025-26 season proved that the hype surrounding Flagg is legitimate. Through 70 games, he averaged 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 4.5 assists on his way to winning the Rookie of the Year award.

The 6-foot-9 forward showed that he could be the Mavericks' franchise cornerstone for a very long time. Still, his emergence does not make the team contenders just yet. Having him simply means they already know who to build around. However, they are likely several years and multiple pieces away from being a title threat.

The Mavericks' current state does not align with Irving's career, given that he is already 34. He can neither wait for Flagg to become a bona fide superstar nor for the Mavericks to find the right pieces to surround him with.

Since their timelines are not in sync, MacMahon believes several teams will keep an eye on this situation. The league insider acknowledged on Monday's episode of "NBA Today" that Irving is still the team's veteran leader. However, that might not be the case for long.

"The question that's being asked around the league is 'for how long?'" MacMahon said. "How long is this fit with Kyrie and the Mavericks?"

MacMahon clarified that the reason is that Flagg is now the team's centerpiece, and not because Irving and the Mavericks no longer see eye to eye.

"Would it make sense for both sides to find a contender for Kyrie to go to?" MacMahon continued. "These are the kind of things that people around the league will be monitoring leading up to the trade deadline."

Spears later added that if they decided to move on from each other, it would be an amicable split. He highlighted the strong relationship between Irving and Mavericks president Masai Ujiri as the reason for this.

"Masai also has a really good relationship, with Kyrie Irving," Spears said. "I think it's the kind of relationship where if Kyrie says, 'hey Masai, like this isn't for me,' I think they could work together to get something done."

Irving has not played a game since March 2025. He suffered a torn ACL near the end of the 2024-25 season, which also kept him out of action for the entirety of last season. He is expected to return this upcoming season, but an exact schedule for it has yet to be officially announced.

Once the nine-time All-Star returns, there's no doubt that he could elevate the Mavericks. He is one of the league's most proficient offensive weapons, and he can take defensive pressure off Flagg.

MORE: 'The Sky Is the Limit' – Mavericks Legend Dirk Nowitzki Details How Cooper Flagg Can Follow In His Footsteps

With Irving running the point, the Mavericks would have someone to keep the team steady through difficult stretches. However, staying could mean sacrificing a chance to add another championship ring to his extensive collection of awards and accolades.

title: Celtic can't sack manager O'Neill, says Lambert
description: Martin O'Neill leaving Celtic would not surprise Paul Lambert, but the former club captain would be "shocked and disappointed" if the veteran manager was to be sacked.
fullText:
Martin O'Neill leaving Celtic would not surprise Paul Lambert, but the former club captain would be "shocked and disappointed" if the manager was to be sacked.

The 74-year-old said he would use the international break to take stock following back-to-back defeats by Rangers.

Those Old Firm setbacks came either side of a home loss to Ferencvaros in the Europa League, while there was a shock Champions League collapse to LASK in August, with a 4-0 aggregate lead surrendered.

"I will reflect on the games," said O'Neill, who was made permanent manager for a second time in the summer after two stints as interim boss last season resulted in a league and Scottish Cup double.

O'Neill, who won another seven trophies with Celtic from 2000-05, when Lambert was playing, added: "I'm not immune from criticism. Absolutely and utterly far from it.

"I think there's every reason to ask 'can you turn this round? Can you change the whole thing?' I have to kind of look at the bigger picture at this minute."

Lambert insists O'Neill is Celtic's best manager since the great Jock Stein, but the 57-year-old added: "It wouldn't surprise me if he left. I don't think he needs it.

"I'd be shocked and disappointed if Celtic sacked him.

"I think they give him the option, if that's what's on his mind, if he did want to walk away.

"He's got enough credit in the bank. It wasn't that long ago people were shouting for a statue for him, so I don't think you can go from one extreme to the other.

"If he wants to go, then he goes himself."

'It might be time to wrap it up' - O'Neill ponders Celtic future after defeat

Rangers look like they know where they want to go - Celtic just look lost

O'Neill steadied the Celtic ship twice last term following the departures of Brendan Rodgers and Wilfried Nancy.

"They were hanging on by a thread and he turned that around," is how former Ipswich Town and Norwich City manager Lambert described the impact of his former boss.

"There was only one person who could rescue Celtic last season and he did that.

"I'd bet any money that he hasn't changed anything from how he was then."

Lambert was critical of individual performances in the defeats by Rangers as well as the remarks of defender Cameron Carter-Vickers, who spoke of playing "too random" and "getting a script and sticking to it".

"The players need to take responsibility," he told BBC Radio Scotland. "I watched the game and dear oh dear...

"That was cringeworthy, the stuff from Carter-Vickers. I thought 'hang on, you're not making a movie'.

"Solve the problem yourselves. When something is not going right, you look to rectify it, you don't look to a manager to say 'do this or do that'.

"I thought that was bang out of order, coming from someone who's been a decent player for Celtic."

title: Sixers 3 goals: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope needs to spark the bench unit
description: Philadelphia 76ers veteran Kentavious Caldwell-Pope needs to bring a spark to the bench unit in an effort to help the team grow.
fullText:
In this new series, Sixers Wire looks at the 16 players, per Spotrac, that comprise the Philadelphia 76ers roster — 14 under standard contracts and the two players on two-way deals — and gives each three goals for the 2026-27 season.

The new season begins on Oct. 20, and training camp is right around the corner. Now is the time to begin previewing the new season of adventure that is Sixers basketball.

Up next in this series is veteran addition Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. The Sixers signed the 13-year man, and 2-time champion, out of Georgia to a deal shortly after landing LeBron James and KCP is expected to bring a lot of experience and shooting to this bench unit. He averaged 8.4 points, 2.7 assists, and 2.5 rebounds for the Memphis Grizzlies in 2025-26.

For Caldwell-Pope, his three goals are as follows:

Caldwell-Pope has been around and seen a lot in this league. The veteran won titles with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020 and the Denver Nuggets in 2023 so he knows what it takes. He knows there will be ups and downs throughout the season, and while the Sixers have plenty of veterans they can turn to in those down moments, Caldwell-Pope has to be the one to settle down a second unit full of younger players. He is somebody who can do a number of different things whether it's a hustle play, knocking down the 3-pointer, or making plays for others. His voice and productivity will be important in the coming season.

Speaking of that 3-pointer, KCP's percentages haven't been great in his previous two seasons. After shooting 40.6% from deep for the Nuggets in 2023-24, that percentage dropped to 34.2% with the Orlando Magic in 2024-25, and then down to 31.6% for the Grizzlies in 2025-26. Granted, the situations with the Magic and Grizzlies were tough as he played for a team that didn't have the shooters and playmakers he played with in Denver, and he could find that touch again in Philadelphia when considering the talent around him now. His 3s will be essential for Philadelphia's success.

Another big aspect Caldwell-Pope brings to the table is his defensive ability. He is someone who really digs in and gets after it on that end of the floor and the Sixers could really use somebody who can step in and produce on both ends of the floor. If Philadelphia can get some legitimate 3-and-D play out of Caldwell-Pope, then the second unit becomes one of the better ones in the league. He is somebody who can adequately defend his man on the perimeter while also being able to switch onto a bigger player if needed.

fullText:
Celtic centre-half Cameron Carter-Vickers has admitted it has been difficult to get all their summer signings "on the same script" but expressed confidence in their squad despite three damaging defeats in a row that have called into question the future of manager Martin O'Neill.

The 74-year-old veteran team boss wondered if it is time "to wrap it up" as he headed into the international break pondering his position at the Scottish Premiership leaders following Sunday's 1-0 defeat by Rangers.

But Carter-Vickers told Sky Sports: "I agree with the manager - I don't think there was much in the game. Neither team were particularly good. There's a lot we can improve on, but I'm confident in the group we have."

Asked why Celtic's season had taken a downturn with two losses to their city rivals either side of Europa League defeat by Ferencvaros, the United States international added: "Hard to put your finger on one thing.

"We played a bit too random. We need to get better at that, getting a script and sticking to it.

"The last two games we've played have been big pressure games. As players, you rely on having something to fall back on.

"We haven't had the time to get that. As players, we can do better for sure. It's something we can improve on.

"There's a lot of new players at the club. It's about getting everyone on the same script. The group are together like we've always been. We need to find consistency."

title: Three Keys For the Miami Heat to Win the Eastern Conference
description: Building around a newly acquired Giannis Antetokounmpo, the Miami Heat must leverage elite interior defense and veteran perimeter shooting to overcome injury concerns and reclaim Eastern Conference dominance this upcoming season.
fullText:
MIAMI, Fla. – As training camp is on the horizon, here are three keys for the Miami Heat to win the Eastern Conference Finals in the 2026-27 NBA season:

Like the popular saying goes, "the best ability is availability." This take primarily falls upon Giannis Antetokounmpo, who played just 36 games last season; a new career low by a significant margin. The 10-time All-Star battled a calf injury and then the Milwaukee Bucks load-managed him. Antetokounmpo, when available last season, averaged 27.6 points on 62.4 percent shooting, 9.8 rebounds, and 5.4 assists.

Also, Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr., two of the Heat's free-agent signings, are over the age of 33. Both sharpshooters will get meaningful playing time, but putting a heavy workload on their shoulders should be taken with precaution.

Given the personnel, the Heat should have one of the best defenses in the league. Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo each received at least five All-Defensive selections. The Heat's new frontcourt duo should be difficult to score over, especially in the paint.

Davion Mitchell and Andrew Wiggins are two underrated defenders who don't get enough credit. They can both guard the perimeter and inside the arc. Despite being undersized (listed at 6'0), Mitchell shouldn't be classified as a lesser matchup. Wiggins, like Antetokounmpo and Adebayo, can guard multiple positions.

Coming off the bench are Bobby Portis Jr. and Pelle Larsson, both of whom are scrappy defenders.

As the saying goes, "defense wins championships." The Heat have the right personnel to live up to the phrase.

After acquiring Antetokounmpo in a blockbuster trade, the Heat needed to surround him with the right pieces, especially outside shooting. As the 31-year-old looks to dominate the paint, he will draw more attention to the defense, creating open looks for others.

Thompson and Hardaway Jr. were critical signees to provide Antetokounmpo floor spacing. Plus, the Heat retained three players (Wiggins, Mitchell, and Simone Fontecchio) who shot over 35 percent from behind the arc last season.

Following an eventful offseason, this team has the components to compete for a championship and win the Eastern Conference Finals. The Heat are among the early favorites, along with the Philadelphia 76ers, New York Knicks, and Boston Celtics. It's been 13 years since the last Larry O'Brien trophy made South Florida its home and a parade went down Biscayne Blvd. The current Heat team is looking to change that.

title: Vikings Give Blunt Harrison Smith Update Ahead of Bears Game
description: Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores opted to ease veteran safety Harrison Smith in the Week 1 win over the Green Bay Packers. fullText:
Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores opted to ease veteran safety Harrison Smith in the Week 1 win over the Green Bay Packers. Smith played 26 snaps, with 19 coming in coverage situations against the Packers, leading to a 48.0 PFF defensive grade.

Smith recorded three pressures, one QB hit, two hurries, and one tackle. Meanwhile, in coverage, the veteran safety allowed two receptions for 27 yards. After missing OTAs, training camp, and the preseason, the Green Bay game let Smith start easing back into action.

On Sept. 15, Flores spoke to the media and shared an update on Smith, including whether he intends to ramp up the veteran's snap count in Week 2 against the Chicago Bears.

"We'll take [Smith's snap count] day-to-day as we put together the game plan," Flores told reporters. "We've been through the early-down portion of it, and we'll get into more of the second and long third down this afternoon, this evening.

"As we start to talk about it, that's when a lot of the play time starts to come alive. Who do we want in this spot [and] who do we want in this spot? Who do we want in this spot? How much of this are we doing? So, I really can't answer that right now, but it was a great first week for him."

While opting for a day-by-day approach to determine Smith's snap count and ease him back into NFL action, Flores praised the veteran's ability to go from not being part of OTAs and training camp to playing an NFL game in a little over a week.

"I don't even know if it was 10 days after he signed, something like that, and so, to go in and play, honestly, I don't even know how many snaps he played, but to go in and play in two-minute situations and third downs and make some plays, I thought it was a good showing," Flores added.

"I certainly couldn't go out there and play a game coming off the street; I thought it was great that he looked good, ran pretty well. And as we go, you just assume he'll get in better shape and be ready for more snaps. But we'll take that day-to-day and see where we're at."

The Vikings will need a fresh, ready-to-make-an-impact Smith, given that they'll face a high-powered Bears offense in Week 2. Recently, Flores spoke with the media about the Bears' offense under head coach Ben Johnson, whom Flores has faced often since Johnson served as the Detroit Lions' offensive coordinator.

"I think the first thing is that all 11 guys are involved," Flores told reporters on Sept. 15. "The receivers are blocking, the tight ends, obviously the offensive line, the quarterback's part of it as far as getting the run going in the right direction wherever that happens to be, based on front, shell coverage versus post-safety coverage.

"There's a lot of different variables, and in some systems, it's, 'Hey, we always do this, or we always do that.' title: Landa wins stage as Mas moves to brink of Vuelta title
description: Spanish cycling enjoys a memorable day at the Vuelta a Espana as veteran Mikel Landa wins the penultimate stage and Enric Mas moves to the brink of the title.
fullText:
Veteran Mikel Landa won the penultimate stage and Enric Mas moved to the brink of the title as Spain enjoyed a memorable day at the Vuelta a Espana.

Mas, 31, stretched his lead over four-time winner Primoz Roglic to more than two minutes - with only the final day, a processional stage, to come.

So as long as the Movistar rider stays upright on Sunday, he will become the first Spaniard to win his country's biggest race since Alberto Contador claimed his third Vuelta title in 2014.

Compatriot Landa, meanwhile, earned his first Grand Tour stage win in nine years and his first in the Vuelta since 2015.

The 36-year-old was part of a three-man breakaway on the queen stage of this year's race, a mountainous 186.8km route from La Calahorra to Collado del Alguacil.

And the Soudal Quick-Step rider went clear on the final climb to cross the line 47 seconds before Norway's Tobias Johannessen.

Felix Gall, who is third overall, took a few seconds out of Mas but otherwise the leader stayed in touch with his general classification rivals, despite repeated attacks from Richard Carapaz.

Sepp Kuss, the 2023 Vuelta winner, spent most of the day between the breakaway and GC group to catapult himself from 11th to fifth overall.

That means Britain's Oscar Onley is now sixth after finishing more than three minutes after Mas, but the 23-year-old is set to win the white jersey for best young rider.

Mas has led since favourite Tadej Pogacar crashed out on stage eight and is poised to win his first Grand Tour after being a Vuelta runner-up three times (2018, 2021 and 2022).

The final stage is a 112km route around Granada which starts outside a supermarket, goes past the Alhambra palace and ends in the Paseo del Salon.

title: Denver Broncos Work Out 3 Versatile Veteran Linebackers on Friday
description: The Denver Broncos might not be done addressing their linebacker and special teams depth if Friday's tryouts are any indication. The post Denver Broncos Work Out 3 Versatile Veteran Linebackers on Friday appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Denver Broncos might not be done addressing the linebacker depth. Three days after they worked out four players (including two linebackers), they again kicked the tires on three 'backers on Friday.

Per the NFL's official transaction wire, they had veterans Cameron Goode, Elliott Brown, and Jahfari Harvey in for tryouts today.

Harvey and Brown both joined the league as undrafted free agents in 2025. Harvey was signed to the Raiders' practice squad (as a defensive end) last season and was called up to compete in two games. He was also re-signed to the practice squad last week but got cut a few days later.

Brown actually began his career in the CFL with the Edmonton Elks in 2023. He stood out from the crowd there (earning CFL West All-Star honors in 2024) over the next two seasons and spent much of last season on the Cardinals' practice squad.

Meanwhile, Goode was drafted by the Dolphins in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He's played in 37 games in Miami, starting two of them, over his first three years. He didn't survive the Dolphins' final roster cuts last week.

Goode might not be a big name, but he's been a key member of the Dolphins' special teams unit since joining the league. He has played 678 snaps in the third phase throughout his career, including 309 snaps (68% of their total special teams snaps) as a rookie and 318 snaps (73%) last season.

Denver Gazette's Chris Tomasson also highlighted Goode, who also has 196 career defensive snaps under his belt, as the most intriguing tryout player.

"Goode is the most notable of the three. He played in 37 games the past three seasons with Miami, with one start. Got in for 14 defensive snaps in Dolphins' infamous 70-20 win over #Broncos in Week 3 in 2023." Tomasson wrote on X.

There is a clear theme among the seven players the Broncos have worked out this week. They're not exactly shopping in the used car section for veterans that could help them on defense (which isn't a surprise, considering how much talent they have on the defensive side of the ball).

Their depth at linebacker is somewhat of a question mark, but they conceivably should feel good about what Red Murdock showed in the preseason in that regard. They could call him up from the practice squad in a pinch if injuries strike.

The players that they've kicked the tires on have three career starts between all seven of them. Most of them do bring special teams experience, though. That could be an area where the Broncos are looking for reinforcements.

They opted not to even bring back undrafted rookie linebacker Taurean York, who also showed some promise on the defensive side of the ball, to the practice squad. Their lack of interest there could be partially due to him struggling in the third phase throughout preseason.

Special teams are an underrated aspect when it comes to team construction. The Broncos might not feel confident in the depth they have in the special teams room (aside from Marvin Mims Jr. providing an elite impact in the return game). That would explain the under-the-radar players they've been looking into.
